reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive defect of ACADS affecting dehydrogenation of short-chain (C4) acyl-CoA substrates in mitochondrial beta-oxidation

Clinical significance is uncertain and debated: many identified individuals are asymptomatic, and it is increasingly regarded as a biochemical phenotype rather than a consistently disease-causing disorder
Two common ACADS variants (c.511C>T and c.625G>A) are susceptibility polymorphisms that lower activity, especially when combined with other factors
Newborn screening hallmark is elevated butyrylcarnitine (C4)
Urine organic acids may show ethylmalonic and methylsuccinic aciduria
Reported but non-specific features have included hypotonia, developmental concerns and feeding difficulties, though causation is often unclear
General supportive metabolic principles apply, including avoidance of prolonged fasting during illness, though rigorous dietary therapy is frequently unnecessary
reference.pathophysiology: Short-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase catalyses the initial dehydrogenation of short-chain (predominantly butyryl-CoA) substrates in the final rounds of mitochondrial beta-oxidation. Reduced activity leads to accumulation of butyryl-CoA and its derivatives, detectable as raised C4 acylcarnitine and as ethylmalonic and methylsuccinic acids in urine. Because short-chain oxidation contributes relatively little to overall energy generation and the block is late in the pathway, the biochemical abnormality often occurs without a clear clinical syndrome, and many carriers of the common variants remain well.
additionalDifferentials: Multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (glutaric aciduria type II)
Isobutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency and other C4-related biochemical findings
Medium-chain and other fatty-acid oxidation defects
Non-specific hypotonia or developmental delay of other cause
Benign biochemical variant with no clinical disease
additionalInvestigations: Plasma acylcarnitine profile showing elevated C4 (butyrylcarnitine)
Urine organic acids seeking ethylmalonic and methylsuccinic aciduria
ACADS molecular genetic testing to distinguish pathogenic variants from common susceptibility polymorphisms
Fibroblast enzyme or flux studies in selected uncertain cases
Assessment to exclude multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency where C4 elevation is marked
redFlags: Marked or combined acylcarnitine abnormalities suggesting multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency rather than isolated SCAD
Progressive encephalopathy raising concern for ethylmalonic encephalopathy
Metabolic decompensation during severe intercurrent illness
Significant neurological regression prompting search for an alternative diagnosis
reference.prognosis: The great majority of screen-detected individuals remain healthy with a normal outlook, and current evidence does not support classifying isolated SCAD deficiency as a reliably harmful disorder; reported symptoms often reflect coincidental or alternative conditions.
pitfalls: Over-diagnosing a disease and imposing unnecessary dietary restriction on an asymptomatic child
Attributing unrelated developmental problems to the biochemical finding
Failing to consider multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency when C4 is only part of a broader abnormal profile
Confusing common susceptibility variants with clearly pathogenic mutations
references: Scriver's OMMBID (Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease)
